sensors.name: left light sensor LLIGHT (light from above, dim inside a tunnel)

control_flow: avoidWalls: if the light is dim, look for a wall on the left or right (turn 20 degrees away from it, else drive on); if bright, call driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if the light is dim, drive forward at 30 %; if bright, call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: curve left on black, curve right otherwise.

likely_intent.description: Drive through a tunnel in dim light without hitting its walls.

decision_points.condition: the left light sensor reads less than 70 % (dim, under a tunnel's roof)

branches.outcome: dim light: it looks for walls on its left and right
bright light: it goes on to the stop-at-wall part

decision_points.condition: in dim light: first an obstacle on the left, second an obstacle on the right

branches.outcome: a wall in front of its left half: it turns left 20 degrees
a wall in front of its right half: it turns right 20 degrees
neither: it drives on in the dark

decision_points.condition: the left light sensor reads less than 70 %

branches.outcome: dim light: it drives forward at 30 %
bright light: it stops at a wall ahead, else follows the line
a wall is ahead: it stops
nothing ahead: it follows the line

uncertainties: You said not to hit the tunnel walls, but not what the robot should do after the tunnel.
In a bend the program turns to the side the wall is on: turning left with a wall in front of its left half may steer it into that wall.
In bright light the program follows the line and stops at a wall ahead, which you didn't mention.
Under the roof it drives on only while the light stays below 70 %: near the openings it does what it does in bright light again.
